title: Thread Stack vs Process Heap Lifetime & Fragmentation

candidate.statement: Thread 1 dynamically allocates a 10MB memory buffer on the heap inside a function, passes a reference pointer to Thread 2, and then exits its function and terminates. (1) Does the buffer remain accessible to Thread 2? (2) Contrast stack frame cleanup vs heap fragmentation.
constraints: Language: C++ / Python / Java memory model

examples.result: Memory valid on heap; invalid if on stack

hints: Remember thread termination destroys thread stack, but process heap belongs to the entire process.
short_diagnostics: Why does heap allocation lead to external fragmentation over time while stack frames do not?

evaluator.reference_solution: (1) Yes, the buffer remains accessible to Thread 2 because the heap belongs to the process, surviving individual thread termination. (2) Stack frames follow strict LIFO automatic allocation/deallocation with zero fragmentation. The heap supports arbitrary sized allocations and out-of-order frees, creating external and internal memory fragmentation over time.
evaluator.rubric: Candidate recognizes process-wide heap survival across thread termination and explains heap fragmentation mechanics.
known_pitfalls: Assuming thread termination frees all memory allocated by that thread.
evaluator.oracle_notes: Reference context from imported CS heap correction.
